Choose R₀>0 with K⊂closedBall(0,R₀) from F001.

value.text: Fix arbitrary t>0, set J=[t/2,3t/2], and choose compact C from H003 so u(x,s)=q for every x∉C and s∈J. To prove Lebesgue measure finite on every compact, fix arbitrary compact K⊂ℝⁿ. By M016, K is bounded. In the Euclidean norm, boundedness implies there is R₀>0 such that every x∈K satisfies ‖x‖≤R₀; record this as F001: ∃R₀>0, ∀x∈K, ‖x‖≤R₀. The local witness will be chosen from this proved existence in the next paragraph.

produces.statement: There exists R₀>0 such that every x∈K satisfies ‖x‖≤R₀.

value.text: Choose R₀ using F001 and define Q=∏_{i=1}^n[-R₀,R₀]. Each coordinate has absolute value at most ‖x‖, hence K⊆Q. M013 and M014 give μ(Q)=∏_{i=1}^n μ([-R₀,R₀])=(2R₀)^n<∞. Since K is compact in the Hausdorff Euclidean space, it is closed and therefore Borel measurable; monotonicity yields μ(K)≤μ(Q)<∞. As K was arbitrary, Lebesgue measure is finite on compact sets. The Borel measurable structure on ℝⁿ is the σ-algebra generated by the Euclidean open sets, so opens are measurable. Joint smoothness and u=q on the open spatial complement of C throughout J imply all first spatial and time derivatives, and the second and mixed derivatives entering e_t, vanish outside C. Thus e(·,t) is continuous with compact support in C. Apply M001 to conclude e(·,t) is integrable. The same smoothness/support argument shows u_t(·,s), u_{x_j}(·,s), e(·,s), and e_t(·,s) are continuous and vanish off C for each s∈J and j=1,…,n. This proves N001 for arbitrary t>0.
